A 226M-parameter from-scratch code LLM got a YaRN context-extension continued pretrain (1000 steps, val loss -8% at 4096 ctx vs 1024, forgetting guard +1.15%). Next we must re-apply instruction SFT (1 epoch, ~19k short instruction/code pairs, lr 3e-5) on top WITHOUT losing the base LM surface: our guard tolerance is +10-15% on the pretraining val loss; a previous full SFT drifted +9.8%, while an in-house LoRA-SFT drifted only +0.13% (at a lower instruction pass-rate 0.90 vs 0.98). Compare strategies: (a) LoRA-SFT with merge afterwards, (b) full SFT mixed with 20-30% pretraining replay tokens, (c) post-hoc weight averaging (model soup / wiSE-FT interpolation) between the fine-tuned model and its own base. Which minimizes forgetting at roughly equal instruction gains, and what ranks, alphas, learning rates and replay ratios does the literature recommend for very small (~0.2B) models?
